Records are timed with TI (60 Hz, 16.7 ms steps) and the interpreter writes one register about every 10 ms: predicted note start error 4 ms mean, 8 ms maximum; the phase of TI adds up to 17 ms, and gate-offs are less exact than note starts. 37 gate-offs shortly before the next note of a voice are written together with that note.

Pulse width modulation, hard restart settings, level and chip volume changes and the title and author are not exported; every instrument uses the hard restart of table row 0 with zero ADSR.
Rows are whole multiples of the row length; note starts and ends are moved to the nearest row.
Rows are one player call long (note starts and ends fall on odd calls): the module is correct but large and uses the fastest tempo.
Note velocities (3 distinct values) are not exported; the module plays at full volume.
The title and the author are not stored in the target.
Cycle numbers are those of SIDWave's engine; a real VICE run of the same SID file starts with its own power-on delay.
